questions.stem: Which of the following is the most important and widely cultivated staple food crop in India, officially feeding more than half of the Indian population?

options.option_text: Wheat
Rice
Maize
Millets

questions.explanation: Rice is the staple food crop of a majority of the people in India. Our country is the second-largest producer of rice in the world after China. It is a kharif crop requiring high temperature and high humidity.

questions.stem: Which specific state in India is currently the largest overall producer of wheat, significantly contributing to the nation's food security?

options.option_text: Punjab (alternative interpretation)
Haryana (alternative interpretation)
Uttar Pradesh
Madhya Pradesh

questions.explanation: While Punjab and Haryana have very high yields per hectare, Uttar Pradesh is the largest producer of wheat in India simply due to the massive land area dedicated to its cultivation in the state.

questions.stem: Which Indian state is traditionally known worldwide as the 'Spice Garden of India' due to its extensive historic production of spices like cardamom, pepper, and cloves?

options.option_text: Karnataka
Tamil Nadu
Andhra Pradesh
Kerala

questions.explanation: Kerala has been a major spice export hub since ancient times (drawing Arab, Portuguese, and Dutch traders). Its tropical climate and hilly terrain (Western Ghats) are perfectly suited for growing a variety of spices.

questions.stem: The term 'Golden Fiber' is popularly used in Indian agriculture and commerce to specifically refer to which important cash crop?

options.option_text: Jute
Cotton
Silk
Hemp

questions.explanation: Jute is known as the golden fiber due to its golden color and its high cash value. It grows well on well-drained fertile soils in the flood plains, primarily in West Bengal, Bihar, and Assam.

questions.stem: Which Indian state is historically the leading producer of soybeans, often officially referred to as the 'Soyabean State' of India?

options.option_text: Maharashtra
Rajasthan (alternative interpretation)
Madhya Pradesh
Gujarat (alternative interpretation)

questions.explanation: Madhya Pradesh has traditionally been the largest producer of soybean in India, often accounting for nearly half of the country's total production, though Maharashtra has recently become a very close competitor.

questions.stem: Sona Masuri (BPT-5204) and Pusa Basmati-1121 are nationally certified improved varieties of which major food crop?

options.option_text: Wheat, cultivated in the Indo-Gangetic plains of northern India
Rice, the principal food crop grown in tropical and subtropical regions
Maize, cultivated both as a food grain and livestock fodder crop
Barley, a rabi cereal grown in cooler semi-arid climatic zones of India

questions.explanation: B is correct because BPT-5204 is the official code for Sona Masuri, a popular medium-grain rice from Andhra Pradesh/Telangana, and Pusa Basmati-1121 is an IARI-developed aromatic long-grain rice—both are rice cultivars. Wheat improved varieties carry names like HD-2967 and PBW-343, making Option A a common but wrong association.

questions.stem: India accounts for approximately 40–45% of global output of which fruit crop, making it the world's undisputed leading producer?

options.option_text: Banana (Musa species), produced widely across India's tropical coastal belts
Papaya (Carica papaya), a year-round tropical orchard fruit grown pan-India
Mango (Mangifera indica), India's officially declared national fruit crop
Guava (Psidium guajava), a high-vitamin C subtropical orchard crop of India

questions.explanation: C is correct because India produces roughly 20–21 million tonnes of mangoes annually, representing about 40–45% of world output. Banana (Option A) is a tempting distractor—India also leads globally in banana output (~27–30% share)—but the ~40–45% figure specifically corresponds to mango, which examiners frequently test.

questions.stem: Coorg Arabica Coffee, which holds a Geographical Indication (GI) tag, is cultivated in high-altitude estates of which Indian state?

options.option_text: Tamil Nadu, where Nilgiris and Kodaikanal harbour significant coffee belts
Karnataka, where Coorg (Kodagu) and Chikkamagaluru districts are located
Kerala, famed for its Wayanad coffee grown under natural forest shade
Andhra Pradesh, home to the tribal Araku Valley coffee plantation belt

questions.explanation: B is correct because Coorg (Kodagu district) and Chikkamagaluru are Karnataka's coffee heartland; the Coorg Arabica Coffee GI tag specifically covers this region. Kerala's Wayanad Coffee (Option C) is a separate GI product, and Tamil Nadu's Nilgiris is better known for tea than coffee GI tags—both are popular distractors.

questions.stem: Under India's Ethanol Blending Programme (EBP), which crop serves as the dominant feedstock through conversion of its by-product molasses?

options.option_text: Maize, a cereal grain increasingly diverted to grain-based ethanol since 2022
Cassava (tapioca), a tropical root crop used in Southeast Asian ethanol plants
Sugarcane, whose sugar-mill molasses supplies the majority of India's ethanol
Sweet sorghum, a drought-hardy energy crop explored for rural biofuel use

questions.explanation: C is correct because sugarcane molasses—the residual syrup after crystallising sugar—is India's primary ethanol feedstock and has powered the EBP since 2003. Maize (Option A) is a growing second-generation feedstock following the 2022 National Biofuel Policy revision, making it the most tempting distractor, but sugarcane still dominates total ethanol volume contributed.

questions.stem: 'Mandua', 'Marua' and 'Nachni' are regional folk names for which calcium-rich millet crop, extensively cultivated in the hill districts of Uttarakhand and Maharashtra?

options.option_text: Pearl Millet (Bajra), the dominant cereal of arid Rajasthan and Haryana belt
Finger Millet (Ragi/Eleusine coracana), the calcium-richest cereal grain known
Sorghum (Jowar), the principal dryland cereal crop grown across the Deccan
Foxtail Millet (Kangni/Setaria italica), cultivated in drier eastern dry tracts

questions.explanation: B is correct because Mandua (Uttarakhand), Marua (Bihar/Jharkhand hills) and Nachni (Maharashtra) are all regional names for Ragi (Finger Millet/Eleusine coracana), which has the highest calcium content among cereals (~344 mg per 100 g). Bajra (Option A) is a common distractor since it is also a minor millet of hill regions, but its folk names are Kambu and Bajri—not Mandua.

questions.stem: India supplies nearly 80–90% of global castor oil exports, a commodity critical to aviation lubricants and pharmaceuticals. Which Indian state dominates castor seed cultivation?

options.option_text: Rajasthan, which leads India in mustard and rapeseed oilseed production volumes
Gujarat, which accounts for over 75% of India's total castor-seed cropped area
Andhra Pradesh, the second-largest castor-growing state behind the national leader
Maharashtra, which leads India in soybean and sunflower oilseed crop cultivation

questions.explanation: B is correct because Saurashtra and North Gujarat regions (Mahesana, Banaskantha) account for over 75% of India's castor-seed acreage; India commands ~80–90% of world castor oil exports. Rajasthan (Option A) is the most tempting distractor because it is also a major oilseed state, but it leads in mustard/rapeseed, not castor. Andhra Pradesh (Option C) is genuinely the second-largest, adding to the difficulty.

questions.stem: Pokkali, a GI-tagged saline-tolerant rice variety cultivated in a seasonal rotation with prawn aquaculture, grows in the coastal wetlands of which Indian state?

options.option_text: Odisha, in the tidal and brackish zones along the Mahanadi coastal delta
West Bengal, in the Sundarbans mangrove and tidal backwater agricultural belt
Kerala, in the low-lying coastal fields of Ernakulam and Thrissur districts
Andhra Pradesh, in the saline Krishna and Godavari river estuarine delta fields

questions.explanation: C is correct because Pokkali is native to coastal Ernakulam and Thrissur in Kerala; it is grown in the kharif season and the same flooded fields shift to brackish-water prawn cultivation in winter—a unique eco-farming cycle that earned it a GI tag. Andhra Pradesh (Option D) is the strongest distractor because it also has saline delta areas with prawn farming, but Pokkali is exclusively associated with Kerala's coastal agro-ecosystem.
